question: A customer is on the release that introduced API v2. Do API responses on that release include the X-RateLimit headers?
expected_answer: No. API v2 arrived in 2.2.0, and in 2.2.0 the X-RateLimit headers were missing (BUG-2200-02). They were fixed in 2.3.0.
evidence: | Introduced | 2.0.0 | 2.2.0 |
Note: in 2.2.0 these headers were missing (BUG-2200-02). Fixed in 2.3.0.

question: We signed on 2026-04-01 and got the release that was current that day. Could we use automatic bank matching right away?
expected_answer: No. Auto-match was added in 2.3.0, released 2026-05-11, so the release current on 2026-04-01 (the 2.2.x line) did not have it.
evidence: | 2.3.0 | Aurora | 2026-05-11 | Automatic bank-reconciliation matching and a custom report builder. |
Added in 2.3.0. Auto-match compares incoming bank transactions with recorded invoices and expenses and suggests matches.

question: Which release fixed the Safari client portal login loop, and was API v2 available in that release?
expected_answer: The loop (BUG-2200-01) was fixed within 2.2.0, and API v2 was introduced in 2.2.0, so yes.
evidence: This affected 2.2.0 and was fixed in a hotfix within 2.2.0. No action needed.
| Introduced | 2.0.0 | 2.2.0 |

question: The release that fixed recurring invoices skipping a cycle: did it also fix the long-invoice PDF problem?
expected_answer: No. 2.3.1 fixed the skipped cycle (BUG-2100-02), but the long-invoice PDF bug (BUG-2310-02) is a known issue in 2.3.1 and is still open.
evidence: BUG-2100-02 — Recurring invoices skip a cycle across DST changes
| BUG-2310-02 | High | Open | Invoices with more than 25 line items export as a single-page PDF, silently dropping remaining line items. |

question: A Professional customer hit their per-minute API limit. What is that limit, and which error code did they get?
expected_answer: 300 requests per minute on Professional; going over returns HTTP 429 with IP-4290 and a Retry-After header.
evidence: | Professional | 300 |
| 429 | IP-4290 | Rate limit exceeded; wait for Retry-After | Yes |

question: Which release has the codename Meridian, and could a customer on it export reports to Excel?
expected_answer: Meridian is 2.2.0. XLSX export arrived in 2.3.0, so on 2.2.0 reports export to PDF and CSV only.
evidence: | 2.2.0 | Meridian | 2026-01-20 | Redesigned client portal, bulk invoice actions, and API v2. |
Before 2.3.0, reports exported to PDF and CSV only.

question: A customer moved from InvoicePilot Classic 1.9.0. Did their late-fee settings carry over, and what can they do instead?
expected_answer: No. Late fee settings do not move, because 2.x has no automatic late fees. They can add a late fee as a separate line item or invoice.
evidence: 2. Late fee settings do not move, because 2.x has no automatic late fees.
In 2.x, add a late fee as a separate line item or a new invoice. Payment reminders can mention your late-fee terms.

question: An integration got IP-4091. What should it do, and will the Python SDK retry it automatically?
expected_answer: Wait about 1 second and retry: the first request with that Idempotency-Key is still running. The Python SDK auto-retries IP-4290, IP-4291, IP-5000, and IP-5030, so IP-4091 is not in its list; handle it yourself.
evidence: | 409 | IP-4091 | A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed | Yes, after 1 second |
The SDK retries IP-4290, IP-4291, IP-5000, and IP-5030 automatically with backoff, up to max_retries times (default 2). It never retries 4xx validation errors.

question: A Starter customer wants webhooks. What is the cheapest plan that includes them, and what does it cost per seat?
expected_answer: Professional, at $25 per seat per year (5 webhook endpoints).
evidence: | Professional | 5 |
| Professional | $25 |

question: Which release introduced credit notes, and could a customer on that release export reports to XLSX?
expected_answer: Credit notes came in 2.2.0. XLSX export arrived in 2.3.0, so no.
evidence: Credit notes were added in 2.2.0 and are available on every plan.
Before 2.3.0, reports exported to PDF and CSV only.

question: We signed on 2025-10-01 and were on the current release that day. Could our clients have received the same payment reminder twice?
expected_answer: Yes. On 2025-10-01 the current release was 2.1.0 (2025-09-16), which had BUG-2100-04: reminders with a send window crossing midnight UTC were sent twice. Fixed in 2.1.1.
evidence: | 2.1.0 | Solstice | 2025-09-16 | Automated recurring invoices and receipt-scanning for expenses. |
This is BUG-2100-04 (Medium). It affected 2.1.0. It was fixed in 2.1.1.

question: A customer's webhook endpoint was down for 2 days. Was the endpoint disabled, and will the events from the first day be resent?
expected_answer: Not disabled: that happens after 3 days of failures. But retries only run for 24 hours (8 attempts), so events from the first day that failed every attempt are not resent.
evidence: If every delivery to an endpoint fails for 3 days, the endpoint is disabled and admins get an email. Re-enable it under Settings > Developer > Webhooks.
Failed deliveries are retried up to 8 times over 24 hours with exponential backoff: after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, 8 hours, and 8 hours.
